newsitem.title: USA: NYSE July 21-25 program trading averages 14.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE July 21-25 program trading averages 14.9 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading for the week of July 21-25 amounted to 14.9 percent of NYSE average daily volume of 550.6 million shares, or 82 million shares a day.
The exchange said buy programs accounted for about 45.1 million of the average 82 million shares a day, and sell programs accounted for about 36.9 million shares during the week.

In all markets, program trading averaged 108 million shares a day during July 21-25. About 75.9 percent of program trading took place on the NYSE, 18.7 percent in non-U.S. markets and 5.4 percent in other domestic markets.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Natwest, Interactive Brokers and Susquehanna Brokerage Services each executed all of their own program activity for customers, as agent. Morgan Stanley split its program trading activity between its own accounts and those of its customers.

Program volume executed on the NYSE by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 76.2 percent during July 21-25. Program volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 21.9 percent of program volume.
Another 1.9 percent was designated as customer facilitation, in which a member firm established or liquidated a principal position to facilitate a program order initiated by a customer.
